text: Listen to me, you coastlands; pay attention, you distant peoples. The LORD called me from the womb; while I was still in my mother's body he spoke my name.
He made my mouth like a sharpened sword; in the shadow of his hand he hid me. He made me a polished arrow and concealed me in his quiver.
He said to me, "You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will show my glory."
But I said, "I have labored in vain; I have spent my strength for nothing, for emptiness. Yet surely my cause rests with the LORD, and my reward with my God."

And now the LORD speaks—he who formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him, so that Israel might be gathered to him; and I am honored in the eyes of the LORD, for my God has been my strength—

he says: "It is too small a thing for you to be my servant, only to restore the tribes of Jacob and bring back those of Israel who are preserved. I will make you a light for the nations, that my salvation may reach to the ends of the earth."

This is what the LORD says—the Redeemer of Israel, his Holy One—to him who is despised, abhorred by the nation, the servant of rulers: "Kings will see and rise, princes will see and bow down, because of the LORD, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you."

versions.text: This is what the LORD says—the Redeemer of Israel, his Holy One—to him who was despised, abhorred by the nations, the servant of rulers: "Kings will see and rise, princes will see and bow down, because of the LORD, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you."
versions.explanation: גּוֹי is singular here ('the nation'), which most naturally refers to the servant's own people; the plural 'the nations' shifts the sense. The participles are also better read as present ('is despised') alongside the following 'servant of rulers.'

text: This is what the LORD says: "In the time of my favor I answered you; on the day of salvation I helped you. I will keep you and make you a covenant for the people, to restore the land and apportion its desolate inheritances,
to say to the captives, 'Come out,' and to those in darkness, 'Show yourselves!' They will graze along the roads and find pasture on every barren height.

versions.text: to say to the captives, 'Come out,' and to those in darkness, 'Be free!' They will graze along the roads and find pasture on every barren height.
versions.explanation: הִגָּלוּ is the niphal imperative of גלה, 'be uncovered / show yourselves,' forming a deliberate contrast with the darkness in which they are hidden. 'Be free!' imports an idea from the previous clause and loses the light/darkness imagery.

text: They will not hunger or thirst, nor will scorching heat or sun strike them down. For he who has compassion on them will guide them and lead them to springs of water.
I will turn all my mountains into a road, and my highways will be raised up.

See, they come from far away—these from the north, these from the west, and these from the land of Syene.[^1]

[^1]: Hebrew "the land of Sinim," likely Syene (Aswan) in the far south of Egypt.

versions.text: See, they come from far away—these from the north, these from the west, and these from the land of Syene.
versions.explanation: 'Syene' is an interpretation of the obscure Hebrew 'Sinim'; a short footnote helps the hearer/reader understand the identification without altering the text.

text: Sing for joy, you heavens; rejoice, you earth; break into song, you mountains! For the LORD has comforted his people and will have compassion on his afflicted ones.
But Zion said, "The LORD has abandoned me; the Lord has forgotten me."
Can a woman forget the child at her breast, or have no compassion on the son she bore? Even if she could forget, I will not forget you.
See, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands; your walls are ever before me.

Your builders hurry back;[^1] those who tore you down and laid you waste depart from you.

[^1]: Or "your sons"; the two words differ only in vowels, and the traditional Hebrew text reads "your sons."

versions.text: Your builders hurry back; those who tore you down and laid you waste depart from you.
versions.explanation: The consonantal text is pointed as 'your sons'; 'your builders' reflects an alternate vocalization supported by an ancient scroll and versions. A footnote preserves the reading of the received text.

text: Lift up your eyes and look around: they are all gathering, they are coming to you. As surely as I live, declares the LORD, you will wear them all like jewelry; you will put them on like a bride.
Though you were ruined and laid waste, your land in rubble, now you will be too small for your people, and those who devoured you will be far away.
The children born in your bereavement will yet say in your hearing, "This place is too cramped for me; make room for me to settle."
Then you will say in your heart, "Who bore me these? I was bereaved and barren, exiled and cast aside—so who raised them? I was left all alone; where have these come from?"
This is what the Lord GOD says: "See, I will lift up my hand to the nations and raise my banner to the peoples; they will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders.

Kings will be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They will bow before you with their faces to the ground; they will lick the dust at your feet. Then you will know that I am the LORD, and that those who hope in me will not be put to shame."

Can plunder be taken from a warrior, or captives rescued from a tyrant?[^1]

[^1]: The traditional Hebrew text reads "from a righteous one"; ancient scroll and version evidence, along with the parallel in the next verse, reads "from a tyrant."

versions.text: Can plunder be taken from a warrior, or captives rescued from a tyrant?
versions.explanation: The rendering 'tyrant' follows the ancient versions and the parallel in v. 25 rather than the received Hebrew text, which reads 'righteous one.' A brief footnote would make this textual choice transparent to the reader.

text: But this is what the LORD says: "Yes, the warrior's captives will be taken, and the tyrant's plunder rescued. I will contend with those who contend with you, and I will save your children.

I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh; they will be drunk on their own blood as with wine. Then all flesh will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob."
